title: Olympus O1 Controlled Learned Baseline
research_question: Does explicit hypothesis to falsification to execution decomposition improve reliable task completion over a monolithic agent when the same learned provider, task set, context, tool access, and budget are used?
hypothesis: Full Olympus improves paired reliable completion by at least five percentage points over the monolithic arm with a paired-bootstrap 95 percent confidence interval lower bound above zero, subject to frozen efficiency and ablation gates.
intended_contribution: A paired four-arm test of the Prometheus to Perseus to Hermes runtime decomposition, falsification, and evidence-enforcement mechanisms under matched information and resource budgets.

development_budget.note: Corrections require a new protocol version and complete rerun.

repositories.name: vertex-studyAI/vertexED.ai
repositories.role: immutable historical evidence and archive surface

claims.claim: The historical O1 protocol has been migrated without scientific-content changes.

decisions: Treat VertexED Olympus PRs as immutable archive/evidence surfaces, not the active implementation branch.
Do not populate missing task, provider, runtime, prompt, decoding, or budget identities by inference.
Do not execute any outcome-bearing arm without a separately reviewed immutable freeze and explicit authorization.
Synthetic contract tests are engineering checks and never O1 evidence.

history.event: Historical four-arm O1 protocol was preregistered in VertexED without an outcome run.
The cumulative nine-file readiness stack was reconciled in VertexED PR 653 at bc22ecc73201659cf099a20b6d038675b7307f28; the PR later closed unmerged.

All nine historical files were copied byte-for-byte into the canonical Olympus repository, bound to SHA-256, and their ten synthetic contract tests passed. Execution remained unauthorized because no task or execution freeze exists.
